topic.title: Text Provenance, Watermarking, and Generated-Content Detection
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: This topic studies how to identify generated text, mark its provenance, and detect whether content entered a model's training data. Watermarks intentionally encode a signal, while passive detectors infer origin from statistical patterns. A representative membership method compares model likelihoods on publicly released and privately retained watermarked rephrasings of the same content.
topic.whyItMatters: Provenance claims require evidence that survives realistic editing and distinguishes different questions: who generated text, whether it was transformed, and whether it was used for training. A detector's benchmark success does not by itself justify certainty about an individual document.
topic.evolution: The representatives connect earlier suspicious-content detection with neural fake-news analysis and modern text watermarking. Recent work studies multibit attribution, semantic-preserving transformations, real-world detector stress tests, and memorized-data removal. Character-level robustness provides related evidence about how altered text is processed.
openQuestions: How can provenance signals survive editing without distorting meaning?
How should uncertainty and false positives be communicated when detection informs consequential judgments?

papers.title: Struct-Bench: A Benchmark for Differentially Private Structured Text Generation
papers.tldr: Struct-Bench uses grammar-described dataset structure to evaluate differentially private synthetic records containing natural language.

papers.title: The Common Pile v0.1: An 8TB Dataset of Public Domain and Openly Licensed Text
papers.tldr: The Common Pile releases eight terabytes of openly licensed text and validates it with two competitively performing 7B language models.

papers.title: Theoretically Grounded Framework for LLM Watermarking: A Distribution-Adaptive Approach
papers.tldr: Joint watermark-and-detector optimization motivates a distribution-adaptive text watermark.

papers.title: Transforming Generic Coder LLMs to Effective Binary Code Embedding Models for Similarity Detection
papers.tldr: Combined supervised training turns generic coder language models into effective binary-code similarity embedding models.

papers.title: Unlearned but Not Forgotten: Data Extraction after Exact Unlearning in LLM
papers.tldr: Access to both pre- and post-unlearning logits enables an extraction attack that challenges privacy assumptions about exact unlearning.

papers.title: What Really is a Member? Discrediting Membership Inference via Poisoning
papers.tldr: Training-data poisoning can undermine membership inference even when membership includes semantic neighbors, exposing an accuracy–robustness tradeoff.

papers.title: Worse than Zero-shot? A Fact-Checking Dataset for Evaluating the Robustness of RAG Against Misleading Retrievals
papers.tldr: RAGuard finds that all tested RAG systems perform worse than their no-retrieval baselines when exposed to potentially misleading retrieved evidence.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Detection of LLM-Generated Text via Implicit Reward Model
papers.tldr: IRM detects LLM-generated text using implicit rewards from existing models, without preference collection or additional training.

papers.title: ACTG-ARL: Differentially Private Conditional Text Generation with RL-Boosted Control
papers.tldr: ACTG-ARL combines private attribute modeling, conditional generation, and anchored reinforcement learning to improve synthetic text quality and control.

papers.title: AlienLM: Alienization of Language for API-Boundary Privacy in Black-Box LLMs
papers.tldr: AlienLM adapts API-accessed models to reversible vocabulary-transformed text, retaining useful performance while resisting the evaluated recovery attacks.

papers.title: AliMark: Enhancing Robustness of Sentence-Level Watermarking Against Text Paraphrasing
papers.tldr: AliMark improves watermark detection after paraphrasing by aligning secret bits against multiple restructured versions of a text.

papers.title: Anchored Decoding: Provably Reducing Copyright Risk for Any Language Model
papers.tldr: Anchored Decoding constrains generation using a permissively trained reference model to improve the trade-off between verbatim copying risk and output quality.

papers.title: Attacks on Machine-Text Detectors Retain Stylistic Fingerprints
papers.tldr: Style-aware attacks evade the tested text detectors, but detectable differences reappear when larger document collections are analyzed.

papers.title: Beyond Heuristic Tuning: Power-Calibrated LLM Watermarking
papers.tldr: A statistical framework selects watermark parameters by explicitly balancing detection power against semantic distortion.

papers.title: Black-Box Detection of LLM-Generated Text Using Generalized Jensen Shannon Divergence
papers.tldr: SurpMark detects machine-generated text by comparing transitions in token surprise with fixed human and machine reference patterns.

papers.title: Block-wise Codeword Embedding for Reliable Multi-bit Text Watermarking
papers.tldr: BREW separates watermark-message recovery from verification to improve reliable detection after local text edits.

papers.title: Catch-22: On the Fundamental Tradeoff Between Detectability and Robustness in LLM Watermarking
papers.tldr: An information-theoretic analysis exposes competing watermark goals and motivates choosing watermark schemes according to expected editing conditions.

papers.title: Characterizing the Effect of Noise in Language Generation in the Limit
papers.tldr: For uniform and non-uniform formal language generation, one noisy example reduces feasibility as much as any finite amount of noise.

papers.title: Copyright-Bench: Agentic Evaluation of Copyright Law Compliance
papers.tldr: Copyright-Bench finds that agents choose infringing content in defined commercial tasks, with some open-weights models becoming less compliant under particular preferences and time pressure.

papers.title: Data Provenance Auditing of Fine-Tuned Large Language Models with a Text-Preserving Technique
papers.tldr: Invisible cue–reply marks enable statistically controlled black-box audits of whether documents were used to fine-tune a language model.

papers.title: Detecting and Filtering Unsafe Training Data via Data Attribution with Denoised Representation
papers.tldr: DRA improves unsafe-data detection by denoising representations before comparing training samples with a small set of unsafe examples.

papers.title: Distinguishable Deletion: Unifying Knowledge Erasure and Refusal for Large Language Model Unlearning
papers.tldr: Distinguishable Deletion uses representation-level energy boundaries to coordinate knowledge removal and refusal in language models.

papers.title: Divergence Decoding: Inference-Time Unlearning via Auxiliary Models
papers.tldr: Divergence Decoding uses small auxiliary models to steer generation away from targeted data and can distill that behavior into the base model.

papers.title: Echoes within the Reasoning: Stealthy and Effective Watermarking via Chain of Thought
papers.tldr: BiCoT embeds ownership signals in reasoning representations and verifies them through token probabilities while preserving reasoning quality in reported tests.

papers.title: EPSVec: Efficient and Private Synthetic Data Generation via Dataset Vectors
papers.tldr: EPSVec privately extracts reusable activation-space steering vectors, enabling efficient synthetic text generation without additional privacy cost per sample.

papers.title: Every Step Counts: Decoding Trajectories as Authorship Fingerprints of dLLMs
papers.tldr: Structural patterns in diffusion language models' decoding trajectories enable source attribution through Gaussian likelihood comparisons.

papers.title: From Weak Cues to Real Identities: Evaluating Inference-Driven De-Anonymization in LLM Agents
papers.tldr: LLM agents can combine weak contextual cues with public evidence to identify anonymized people, sometimes even without an explicit re-identification request.

papers.title: How Good is Post-Hoc Watermarking With Language Model Rephrasing?
papers.tldr: Rephrasing-based watermarking shows strong results on open-ended text, but struggles with code and does not consistently benefit from larger models.

papers.title: IACW: Intent-Aware Controllable Watermarking for Scalable Authorial Intent Attribution
papers.tldr: IACW embeds intent-sensitive watermarks to distinguish AI editing from generation while maintaining near-unwatermarked semantic fidelity.

papers.title: Ideal Attribution and Faithful Watermarks for Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper defines ideal attribution rules from interaction histories and frames watermarking as faithfully implementing those rules.

papers.title: ImpText: A Benchmark and Tool-Augmented Framework for Implicit Text Reasoning
papers.tldr: ImpText benchmarks deliberately concealed text and introduces a tool-assisted reader that improves recognition and robustness in adversarial settings.

papers.title: IPMark: A Sentence-Level Watermark for LLMs with Hierarchical Personalization and Efficient Detection
papers.tldr: IPMark combines sentence-level semantic and syntactic watermarking with hierarchical model and user identities for efficient personalized attribution.

papers.title: Leak@$k$: Unlearning Does Not Make LLMs Forget Under Probabilistic Decoding
papers.tldr: Leak@k exposes information that resurfaces after unlearning under repeated probabilistic sampling, while RULE improves robustness on evaluated benchmarks.

papers.title: Less is More: Geometric Unlearning for LLMs with Minimal Data Disclosure
papers.tldr: Geometric Unlearning aligns hidden states with a compact reference subspace to suppress targets using minimal synthetic data.

papers.title: Linear Ensembles Wash Away Watermarks: On the Fragility of Distributional Perturbations in LLMs
papers.tldr: WASH averages output probabilities across models to attenuate text watermarks, exposing a vulnerability when provider-specific perturbations cancel.

papers.title: LLM Self-Recognition: Steering and Retrieving Activation Signatures
papers.tldr: Sparse internal steering creates recoverable model-attribution fingerprints, achieving over 98% detection accuracy across tested settings while preserving text quality.

papers.title: LLM Watermark Evasion via Bias Inversion
papers.tldr: Bias-inversion rewriting exploits sensitivity in watermark token statistics, exceeding 99% evasion across tested schemes while better preserving meaning than prior baselines.

papers.title: LORD-GoF: A Robust Online Detection Approach for LLM Watermarks in Sparse and Mixed Streams
papers.tldr: LORD-GoF dynamically adjusts watermark-detection thresholds to control online false discoveries in sparse streams mixed with human writing.

papers.title: NExT-Guard: Streaming Safeguard without Token-Level Labels
papers.tldr: NExT-Guard uses sparse-autoencoder features to monitor streaming safety without token-level training labels.

papers.title: On the Salience of Low-Probability Tokens for AI-Generated Text Detection: A Multiscale Uncertainty Perspective
papers.tldr: Uncertainty detects AI-generated text by combining local and distribution-level measurements of informative low-probability tokens.

papers.title: PASA: A Principled Embedding-Space Watermarking Approach for LLM-Generated Text under Semantic-Invariant Attacks
papers.tldr: PASA places watermarks in semantic embedding space and shows robustness to strong paraphrasing while preserving text quality.

papers.title: PEARL: Differentially Private and Entropy-Aware Regulated Language Generation
papers.tldr: PEARL uses confidence-gap-guided private decoding to improve resistance to personal-information extraction while reducing hallucination in experiments.

papers.title: Position: The Data Provenance–Parametric Divide in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper proposes separating LLM generation from factual authorization, allowing claims only when traceable supporting evidence is available.

papers.title: Privasis: Synthesizing the Largest "Public" Private Dataset from Scratch
papers.tldr: Privasis provides 1.4 million synthetic sensitive-information records and supports compact sanitization models that outperform the compared larger models.

papers.title: Provable Training Data Identification for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: PTDI identifies sets of likely training examples with provable false identification rate control using known unseen data.

papers.title: Rethinking Pretraining Data Detection for LLMs: From Local to Global
papers.tldr: AECA detects possible pretraining membership from sequence-wide probability dynamics, improving WikiMIA results especially for long texts.

papers.title: RLCracker: Evaluating the Worst-Case Vulnerability of LLM Watermarks with Adaptive RL Attacks
papers.tldr: RLCracker shows that adaptive reinforcement-learning paraphrasing can undermine text watermarks with limited examples and no detector access.

papers.title: Selective Disclosure Watermarking for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: HeRo distributes watermark metadata across vocabulary hierarchy layers so verifiers can decode only the portions permitted by their access level.

papers.title: Stability-Aware Feature Design for Robust Watermark Detection in Machine-Generated Text
papers.tldr: Pattern Stability Score improves watermark detection by combining local text statistics with their stability across repeated paraphrasing.

papers.title: Telescope: Improving Zero Shot Detection of LLM Generated Content By Measuring Token Repetition Probability
papers.tldr: Telescope Perplexity uses token-repetition probabilities as an efficient signal for zero-shot detection of model-generated writing.

papers.title: Towards Reliable Marking and Verification of AI-Generated Text via Geometry-aware Sentence-level Watermarking
papers.tldr: X-Guard improves sentence-level text watermarking by aligning embedding geometry with semantic regions used for watermark injection.

papers.title: Understanding the Ability of LLMs to Handle Character-Level Perturbation
papers.tldr: Many language models retain notable comprehension under severe character corruption, showing resilience to fragmented tokenization and disrupted text segmentation.
